sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In 1898, China granted a 99-year lease to Great Britain for the areas across the harbor
sentences.zh: 在1898年，中国将海港对岸的地区

sentences.en: from the British-controlled island of Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 租借给英国九十九年，对岸即英国控制的香港岛。

sentences.en: But smack in the middle of that territory, known as Kowloon,
sentences.zh: 但在该领土正中央，也就是被称为九龙的地方，

sentences.en: was an enclave that wasn't included in the lease.
sentences.zh: 有一个并未包含在租借范围内的飞地。

sentences.en: A place that would, at least officially, still be controlled by the Chinese.
sentences.zh: 一个至少在官方上仍然由中国控制的地方。

sentences.en: It was a large fort, built decades earlier,
sentences.zh: 这是一座几十年前建造的大型堡垒，

sentences.en: to put a check on British expansion.
sentences.zh: 旨在遏制英国的扩张。

sentences.en: But it evolved into something very, very different.
sentences.zh: 但它演变成了一个截然不同的存在。

sentences.en: This was the first photo that I saw of it.
sentences.zh: 这是我看到的关于它的第一张照片。

sentences.en: Why don't you start describing it?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不开始描述它呢？

sentences.en: I haven't taken it in yet.
sentences.zh: 我还没完全消化呢。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: The first analogy that springs into my mind is it looks a little bit like the Borg cube from Star Trek.
sentences.zh: 我脑海中涌现的第一个类比是，它看起来有点像《星际迷航》里的博格方块。

sentences.en: It's a city block,
sentences.zh: 它是一个城市街区，

sentences.en: and we're not looking at a neighborhood that's nestled in a city.
sentences.zh: 而我们看到的并不是一个坐落于城市中的社区。

sentences.en: Like, we're looking at a Borg cube that is in the middle of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们看到的是一个远在荒郊野岭的博格方块。

sentences.en: There's skyscrapers behind it,
sentences.zh: 它身后有摩天大楼，

sentences.en: but the demarcation between this neighborhood and everything else is staggering.
sentences.zh: 但这个社区与周围一切的界限却令人震惊。

sentences.en: That's my friend Nick Vanderkolk from the program Love & Radio showing me photos.
sentences.zh: 那是我的朋友尼克·范德科尔克，来自《爱与广播》节目，正在给我看照片。

sentences.en: He was the first person who told me about this place.
sentences.zh: 他是第一个跟我提起这个地方的人。

sentences.en: It became known as Kowloon Walled City.
sentences.zh: 它后来被称为九龙城寨。

sentences.en: And even though the walls eventually came down, its name was still appropriate.
sentences.zh: 尽管城墙最终被拆除，但这个名字依然贴切。

sentences.en: There was no mistaking the boundaries between it and the rest of Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 它与香港其余地区的界限毋庸置疑。

sentences.en: The edges became a wall of 13-story high-rises overlooking a comparatively sparse squatter's village.
sentences.zh: 边缘变成了一堵由十三层高楼组成的墙，俯瞰着相对稀疏的寮屋村。

sentences.en: Buildings evolved organically,
sentences.zh: 建筑自然生长，

sentences.en: growing tendrils of bridges, pipes, and wires that encroached on other buildings,
sentences.zh: 延伸出侵占其他建筑的桥梁、管道和电线藤蔓，

sentences.en: until the city turned into a single, giant organism.
sentences.zh: 直到整座城市变成了一个巨大的单一有机体。

sentences.en: Because it was in this legal no-man's land,
sentences.zh: 因为它处于这片法律三不管地带，

sentences.en: not under British jurisdiction, but pretty much ignored by the Chinese authorities,
sentences.zh: 既不受英国司法管辖，又基本上被中国当局忽视，

sentences.en: it became a magnet for the displaced and the marginal.
sentences.zh: 它成了流离失所者和边缘人群的磁石。

sentences.en: Thousands of people moved there after war with Japan broke out in the 30s,
sentences.zh: 上世纪30年代抗日战争爆发后，数千人搬到那里，

sentences.en: and even more moved there after the Republic of China went communiSt.
sentences.zh: 而随着中华民国走向共产主义，更多人搬了进去。

sentences.en: It attracted gangsters, drug addicts, sex workers, refugees,
sentences.zh: 它吸引了歹徒、瘾君子、性工作者、难民，

sentences.en: and it also drew a lot of average people from all over China who needed cheap rent and saw opportunity.
sentences.zh: 它还吸引了来自中国各地、需要廉价租金并看到机会的许多普通人。

sentences.en: Kowloon Walled City was, at its height, the densest place anywhere, ever.
sentences.zh: 九龙城寨在其鼎盛时期，是史上人口最稠密的地方。

sentences.en: It had a population density of about 3.2 million people per square mile.
sentences.zh: 它的人口密度约为每平方英里320万人。

sentences.en: In comparison, Manhattan has a population density of about 70,000 people per square mile.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，曼哈顿的人口密度约为每平方英里7万人。

sentences.en: That means that Kowloon Walled City was about 46 times as dense as Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 这意味着九龙城寨的人口密度大约是曼哈顿的46倍。

sentences.en: So let me put that another way.
sentences.zh: 我换个方式表达吧。

sentences.en: If Manhattan wanted to get anywhere close to that kind of density,
sentences.zh: 如果曼哈顿想要达到那种人口密度，

sentences.en: every man, woman, and child living in Texas would have to move there.
sentences.zh: 所有居住在得克萨斯州的男人、女人和儿童都必须搬到那里。

sentences.en: I came across it very much by accident.
sentences.zh: 我非常偶然地遇到了它。

sentences.en: I came around one corner and saw this structure that looked really different than everything else around it.
sentences.zh: 我转过一个街角，看到了这个结构，它看起来与周围的一切截然不同。

sentences.en: That's Greg Girard, a photographer.
sentences.zh: 那是摄影师格雷格·吉拉德。

sentences.en: He lived in Hong Kong in the 80s and 90s.
sentences.zh: 他在80和90年代住在香港。

sentences.en: And that's when I first became aware of the Walled City and started photographing there.
sentences.zh: 也就是那时我第一次知道城寨并在那里拍照。

sentences.en: It's density was immediately apparent.
sentences.zh: 它的密度显而易见。

sentences.en: Buildings had been built up against each other without any space between them.
sentences.zh: 建筑彼此紧挨着建造，中间没有任何空间。

sentences.en: Each homeowner or each person who rented would build a different kind of caged balcony
sentences.zh: 每个房主或租房者都会建造不同种类的鸟笼式阳台，

sentences.en: that would stick out a meter or two from their apartment.
sentences.zh: 从他们的公寓向外凸出一两米。

sentences.en: It was a way of opening up the apartment and getting more space and air and light.
sentences.zh: 这是一种打开公寓、获取更多空间、空气和光线的方法。

sentences.en: I went for a first walk into one of the alleys and was immediately struck by what's overhead.
sentences.zh: 我第一次走进其中一条小巷，立刻就被头顶的景象震撼了。

sentences.en: And that's this tangle of electrical wires and wet garbage that had been thrown from the upper floors.
sentences.zh: 那是纠缠在一起的电线和从高层扔下来的湿垃圾。

sentences.en: TV antennas all over the place.
sentences.zh: 到处都是电视天线。

sentences.en: Incredible noises from the various manufacturing, metalwork, small kind of foundries,
sentences.zh: 各种制造业、金属加工、小型铸造厂发出的令人难以置信的噪音，

sentences.en: cotton mills, kitchens, furnaces burning for barbecuing pork or duck or whatever.
sentences.zh: 棉纺厂、厨房、用于烧烤猪肉、鸭肉或任何东西的燃烧熔炉。

sentences.en: Sensations underfoot as you go down some alleys, you know, into watery, squishy stuff.
sentences.zh: 当你走进一些小巷时，脚下的感觉你知道，踩在湿漉漉、黏糊糊的东西上。

sentences.en: Watery, squishy stuff?
sentences.zh: 湿漉漉、黏糊糊的东西？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, you know, stuff between buildings that you're walking on.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，你知道，建筑之间你踩着的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, I really don't even know what some of it was.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我甚至真的不知道其中一些是什么。

sentences.en: All manner of sensory assault, really.
sentences.zh: 简直是全方位的感官袭击。

sentences.en: Greg took a lot of photographs of the Walled City.
sentences.zh: 格雷格拍了很多关于城寨的照片。

sentences.en: There's one, probably one of my favorites of his, of a temple.
sentences.zh: 有一张，可能是我最喜欢他的照片之一，拍的是一座寺庙。

sentences.en: It's much shorter than the 13-story high-rises around it.
sentences.zh: 它比周围13层的住宅楼矮得多。

sentences.en: Over the temple is this huge metal grate that's there to keep trash off the roof.
sentences.zh: 寺庙上方是一个巨大的金属网格，用来防止垃圾落到屋顶上。

sentences.en: The lifestyle of living in the Walled City was to dispose of garbage by throwing it out your window.
sentences.zh: 城寨里的生活方式是通过把垃圾扔出窗外来处理垃圾。

sentences.en: And so the temple built a big net above its roof.
sentences.zh: 所以寺庙在屋顶上方搭建了一个大网。

sentences.en: And then it actually cast beautiful shadow through all this trash.
sentences.zh: 然后它实际上通过所有这些垃圾投射出美丽的阴影。

sentences.en: It allowed for a really interesting light to filter down through some of the bases in the garbage,
sentences.zh: 它让一些光线穿过垃圾底部的空隙透射下来，

sentences.en: almost like a tropical kind of canopy, except this one was made of refuse.
sentences.zh: 几乎就像某种热带树冠，只不过这个是由废弃物制成的。

sentences.en: That new voice you heard is Aaron Tan.
sentences.zh: 你听到的那个新声音是陈浩能。

sentences.en: Aaron is an architect from Hong Kong and wrote his master's thesis about the Walled City.
sentences.zh: 陈浩能是一位来自香港的建筑师，他关于城寨写了硕士论文。

sentences.en: And he interviewed a lot of people who lived there.
sentences.zh: 他采访了许多住在那里的人。

sentences.en: The Walled City was, at its prime time, is during the 60s and 70s.
sentences.zh: 城寨的黄金时期是在60和70年代。

sentences.en: And that was also the same time where the great thinkers of architects, like the Archigrams, the Metabolists,
sentences.zh: 这也是建筑界的伟大思想家们，比如“建筑电讯派”、新陈代谢派，

sentences.en: was talking about this kind of self-organizing structure, intelligent building thinking.
sentences.zh: 在谈论这种自组织结构、智能建筑思想的同一时期。

sentences.en: All these things are going on in the West, but not recognizing the existence of the Walled City actually is doing that.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情都在西方发生，却没有认识到城寨的存在实际上正在这样做。

sentences.en: So on the other hand, the Walled City in Hong Kong is growing by itself, but without any architect working on it.
sentences.zh: 所以另一方面，香港的城寨在自行生长，但没有任何建筑师在上面工作。

sentences.en: So it's like the coexistence of two.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像两者的共存。

sentences.en: One is very theoretical, one is something very real, and they do not know the existence of each other
sentences.zh: 一个是高度理论化的，一个是十分现实的，它们彼此并不知道对方的存在，

sentences.en: until much later, in the late 80s, when Greg Girard or in the early 90s,
sentences.zh: 直到很久以后，在80年代末或90年代初，

sentences.en: when we start to look at it and see the amazing coexistence of these two things during the same time.
sentences.zh: 当我们开始研究它，并看到这两种事物在同一时期惊人的共存时。

sentences.en: Because the Walled City was virtually autonomous from both China and Britain,
sentences.zh: 由于城寨对中国和英国而言实际上是自治的，

sentences.en: there wasn't a lot in the way of infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 这里几乎没有什么基础设施。

sentences.en: There weren't any building codes, obviously, and there wasn't any garbage collection either.
sentences.zh: 显然没有任何建筑规范，也没有任何垃圾收集。

sentences.en: Which is why people threw their trash out the window.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们把垃圾扔出窗外。

sentences.en: The Walled City gained a reputation as a sort of den of iniquity.
sentences.zh: 城寨赢得了罪恶渊薮的声誉。

sentences.en: There were high levels of prostitution, gambling, organized crime,
sentences.zh: 这里有高水平的卖淫、赌博、有组织犯罪，

sentences.en: and for some reason there seems to be a lot of rampant, unlicensed dentistry.
sentences.zh: 而且不知为何，这里似乎有很多猖獗的无证牙医。

sentences.en: But a kind of order did emerge.
sentences.zh: 但某种秩序确实出现了。

sentences.en: The Triads, who are sort of like the Chinese version of the Mafia,
sentences.zh: 三合会，有点像中国版的黑手党，

sentences.en: filled the power vacuum with its own rule of law.
sentences.zh: 用自己的法治填补了权力真空。

sentences.en: They made at least some attempts at hygiene.
sentences.zh: 他们在卫生方面至少做出了一些尝试。

sentences.en: Triad gangs could get the drug addicts to clean up the streets.
sentences.zh: 三合会帮派会找瘾君子来清理街道。

sentences.en: And residence organizations popped up to settle disputes between neighbors.
sentences.zh: 居民组织也应运而生，以解决邻里之间的纠纷。

sentences.en: There was industry too.
sentences.zh: 这里也有工业。

sentences.en: Noodle factories, fishball factories, textiles.
sentences.zh: 面条厂、鱼蛋厂、纺织厂。

sentences.en: There were restaurants, and because the sanitation wasn't great,
sentences.zh: 这里有餐馆，而且由于卫生状况不是很好，

sentences.en: they would kill your meal in front of you to prove that they weren't serving you spoiled meat.
sentences.zh: 他们会当着你的面把你要吃的动物宰杀，以证明他们卖的不是变质肉。

sentences.en: A lot of the electricity was pirated.
sentences.zh: 大部分电力都是偷接的。

sentences.en: Someone would tap a cable into the grid and run it over and across the buildings.
sentences.zh: 有人将电缆搭接到电网并将其拉过建筑。

sentences.en: And then an official would shut it off.
sentences.zh: 然后官员会将其切断。

sentences.en: Then somebody would tap the grid again, lay a new cable on top of the dead one,
sentences.zh: 接着有人会再次接入电网，在废弃的电缆上铺设新电缆，

sentences.en: and then that would get shut off, and so on and so on.
sentences.zh: 然后这根电缆又会被切断，周而复始。

sentences.en: Eventually there were just so many cables running over and across all the buildings
sentences.zh: 最终，有太多的电缆在所有建筑物上方和穿梭，

sentences.en: that the alleyways below were almost in total darkness.
sentences.zh: 以至于下方的小巷几乎处于完全黑暗之中。

sentences.en: You cannot rely on what you see because you get lost right away, you know.
sentences.zh: 你不能依赖你所看到的，因为你会马上迷路，你知道的。

sentences.en: But based on smell, you could better.
sentences.zh: 但根据气味，你可以做得更好。

sentences.en: Maybe they're selling pork here, and then there's another cluster of factories doing sugar and sweet.
sentences.zh: 也许他们这里在卖猪肉，然后是另一群做糖果的工厂。

sentences.en: So actually relying on your smell, you can actually navigate through the city better.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上依靠你的嗅觉，你可以更好地在城市中穿行。

sentences.en: It was said that if you knew your way around the city's elaborate maze of catwalks,
sentences.zh: 据说，如果你熟悉城寨复杂的走道迷宫，

sentences.en: you could walk from one side to the other without ever touching the ground.
sentences.zh: 你可以从一头走到另一头，而双脚从不着地。

sentences.en: In the 70s and 80s, when the end of the new territory's lease was on the horizon,
sentences.zh: 在70和80年代，当新界租约临近尾声时，

sentences.en: Britain and China began to figure out what it meant for the future of Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 英国和中国开始摸索这对香港的未来意味着什么。

sentences.en: And part of that negotiation included the question of what to do with the walled city.
sentences.zh: 而谈判的一部分就包括如何处理城寨的问题。

sentences.en: After three quarters of a century of ambiguity from both countries,
sentences.zh: 在两国经历了四分之三世纪的含糊其辞之后，

sentences.en: they finally agreed on a long eviction process.
sentences.zh: 他们终于就一个漫长的驱逐程序达成一致。

sentences.en: And in 1993, four years before Britain handed over control of Hong Kong to China,
sentences.zh: 1993年，即英国将香港控制权移交中国前四年，

sentences.en: Kowloon walled city was demolished.
sentences.zh: 九龙城寨被拆除了。

sentences.en: But the story of the walled city does not end with its destruction.
sentences.zh: 但城寨的故事并没有随着它的毁灭而结束。

sentences.en: I'm Brian Douglas, and I designed the first draft of the Kowloon walled city level in Call of Duty Black Ops.
sentences.zh: 我是布赖恩·道格拉斯，我设计了《使命召唤：黑色行动》中九龙城寨关卡的第一版草图。

sentences.en: Call of Duty is a first-person shooter video game series.
sentences.zh: 《使命召唤》是一个第一人称射击电子游戏系列。

sentences.en: Normally you get into like an army situation where
sentences.zh: 通常你会进入一种军队情境，

sentences.en: maybe you're in the middle of the street or you're up on the second story or something.
sentences.zh: 也许你在街道中央，或者在二楼之类的地方。

sentences.en: But it's not a very vertically dynamic world most of the time,
sentences.zh: 但大多数时候它不是一个垂直动态很强的世界，

sentences.en: except visually, but we never usually get to get up to those tall points.
sentences.zh: 除了视觉上，但我们通常无法到达那些高处。

sentences.en: In other words, in most games like this, the scenery is just scenery.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，在大多数这种游戏中，风景只是风景。

sentences.en: You can't interact with most of the visual world that exists off the ground.
sentences.zh: 你无法与地面之外的大多数视觉世界进行交互。

sentences.en: Usually they're just there to make the world feel fleshed out and real.
sentences.zh: 通常它们只是为了让世界感觉饱满和真实。

sentences.en: But with Kowloon, it was actually like, well, let's go up there.
sentences.zh: 但在九龙，实际上是，嗯，让我们去上面看看。

sentences.en: Call of Duty Black Ops is just one of many games to recreate the city.
sentences.zh: 《使命召唤：黑色行动》只是重现这座城市的众多游戏之一。

sentences.en: It lives on in a kind of virtual memorial,
sentences.zh: 它以一种虚拟纪念碑的形式永存，

sentences.en: except with way more gunfire.
sentences.zh: 只不过伴随着更多的枪声。

sentences.en: This is kind of a level builder's dream because
sentences.zh: 这可以说是关卡设计者的梦想，因为

sentences.en: it provides opportunities that we don't normally get.
sentences.zh: 它提供了我们通常无法获得的机会。

sentences.en: In our first sequence, you can see sort of the liberties that it allowed us to take
sentences.zh: 在我们的第一个序列中，你可以看到它允许我们采取的某种自由度，

sentences.en: because if I needed to just make something really sort of crooked and awkward,
sentences.zh: 因为如果我需要把某些东西做得很歪扭、很尴尬，

sentences.en: it was just all like carte blanche because it really fit into the nature of the city.
sentences.zh: 这完全是全权处理，因为它真的很符合城市的性质。

sentences.en: The doorways weren't necessarily the right size,
sentences.zh: 门的大小不一定合适，

sentences.en: or the hallways were a little thinner and they'd bend in the middle.
sentences.zh: 或者走廊有点窄，在中间弯曲。

sentences.en: Some of the ceilings were a little taller where it wasn't really fully developed
sentences.zh: 有些天花板在尚未完全开发的地方稍微高一些，

sentences.en: and there were wires coming off of it.
sentences.zh: 上面还垂着电线。

sentences.en: You could just imagine what you will for it, and it was probably suitable.
sentences.zh: 你可以随心所欲地想象它的样子，而且它可能都很合适。

sentences.en: I played the walled city level.
sentences.zh: 我玩过城寨这个关卡。

sentences.en: Actually, that's a lie.
sentences.zh: 其实那是谎言。

sentences.en: I watched a friend of a friend play because I probably would have died in the first two minutes.
sentences.zh: 我看着朋友的朋友玩，因为我大概在前两分钟就死了。

sentences.en: But anyway, it's clear that Brian and the other designers put a lot of thought into each location.

sentences.en: For instance, a particular room might have a half-eaten meal on the table.
sentences.zh: 例如，某个房间的桌子上可能摆着一份吃了一半的饭菜。

sentences.en: There are these signs of a moment in someone's life.

sentences.en: But even though the world is full of bad guys trying to shoot you,
sentences.zh: 但尽管世界上到处都是想朝你开枪的坏蛋，

sentences.zh: 你却几乎遇不到任何一个真正生活在那里的人。

sentences.en: It's easy to lose sight of the fact that this was a real, living, breathing neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 人们很容易忽视这样一个事实：这曾是一个真实、鲜活、有呼吸的社区。

sentences.en: When you discovered that they were going to be tearing down,

sentences.en: You sort of knew it as a real neighborhood,

sentences.en: and not just this sort of fantastical den of iniquity.

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: You know, quite mixed feelings.

sentences.en: and it was just this fantastic phenomenon.

sentences.en: This is Greg Gerard again, the photographer.

sentences.en: At the same time, that civic-minded part of you knows that this canton shouldn't continue.

sentences.en: Aaron, the architect, has a similar ambivalence.

sentences.zh: 但对亚伦来说，将它拆除是有价值的。

sentences.en: a way to see how the various pieces of the city all fit together.
